title: `AVG` of doubles: plain sum by the count
description: `AVG(DOUBLE)` is the plain sequential sum (duckdb-sum-double) divided by the count; `favg` uses the Kahan sum (duckdb-kahan-sum).

Order class: (a) the sum of duckdb-sum-double (sequential per state, partials merged in finishing order, a constant run as one product), then one division by the count (`state.value / state.count`, the count exact as a double). (b) γ_{h+1} Σ|x_i| / n on the mean, h as for the sum (at most n − 1), so at most γ_n Σ|x_i| / n (Higham §4.2 for the sum, one more rounding for the quotient); within #85's `avgTolScaled`, which allows γ_{n+2}. (c) The source below; `avg(0.1)` over 10 constant rows is 0.1, where the sequential sum gives 0.09999999999999999. (d) `AggFn.avg` is the `sum_order` choice divided by n, so this refines SEQUENTIAL at one thread without constant vectors and ANY otherwise, with the same open point for a constant run's product.

evidence.sql: SET threads = 1; SELECT sum(0.1::DOUBLE)::VARCHAR, avg(0.1::DOUBLE)::VARCHAR, fsum(0.1::DOUBLE)::VARCHAR FROM range(10); CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT 0.1::DOUBLE v FROM range(10); SELECT sum(v)::VARCHAR, fsum(v)::VARCHAR FROM t; SELECT sum(v ORDER BY i)::VARCHAR FROM (SELECT 0.1::DOUBLE v, i FROM range(10) r(i))
evidence.observed: constant argument: sum 1.0, avg 0.1, fsum 1.0; table column: sum 0.9999999999999999, fsum 1.0; sum(v ORDER BY i) 0.9999999999999999. 0.1 * 10 is 1.0 in double, the ten additions in turn 0.9999999999999999
